newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rice exports firm on African demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian rice exports firm on African demand.

text.p: A surge in demand from African countries stoked Indian rice exports during the past week, traders said on Thursday.

"We have signed contracts to export 50,000 tonnes of lower grades of rice to African countries in the past three days," Prem Garg, managing director of Sri Lal Mahal Overseas Ltd, a leading Delhi foodgrains exporter, told Reuters.
Garg said the contracts were mainly for 25 percent broken and 100 percent broken non-Basmati rice.
Traders said five percent broken non-Basmati rice was quoted at $295 per tonne FOB, 10 percent at $285, 15 percent at $250, 25 percent at $235 and 100 percent at $170 per tonne.
Exporters said the Philippines was in the market for nearly 700,000 tonnes of rice, and they were expecting to sell substantial quantities to them.
"We expect to sell to them around 50,000 to 100,000 tonnes of rice, mainly 25 percent broken," said Rajeev Kumar, export manager of ITC Ltd, a leading Delhi foodgrains exporter.
Kumar said that last year the Philippines had brought rice from India, but it was mainly from the government agencies.
"But this time we hope they buy from private traders," he said.
Kumar said exporters were currently negotiating export contracts of around 50,000 tonnes of 100 percent broken rice to African countries.
He said nearly 20,000 tonnes of Basmati rice were going to Saudi Arabia every month. "Saudi Arabia is the main market we are concentrating on for our Basmati rice exports," Kumar said.
